statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-105326 (GHSA-r4wf-366f-f6g3): in OpenPrinting CUPS 2.4.7 to 2.4.19, the scheduler accepts any address in a mailto: notify-recipient-uri and the mailto notifier passes it to sendmail as a command-line argument, so a recipient beginning with '-' is read as a sendmail option; with a traditional sendmail that honours -C this can lead to command execution as the CUPS filter user. It is fixed in CUPS 2.4.20 by validating notification addresses in notifier/mailto.c: https://github.com/OpenPrinting/cups/security/advisories/GHSA-r4wf-366f-f6g3, https://github.com/OpenPrinting/cups/commit/611d1bd3bdf832363832383567906a6d7fd6c47d. The DHI cups package for Alpine 3.24, which holds the scheduler and the notifiers, is published at 2.4.18-r0 (aarch64 only), 2.4.19-r0, 2.4.20-r0, 2.4.20-r1 and 2.4.20-r2 (x86_64 and aarch64). Checked /usr/lib/cups/notifier/mailto in each: 2.4.18-r0 and 2.4.19-r0 still carry the old 'Bad recipient' check, and every 2.4.20 build carries the new address validation ('Bad '%s' email address', 'Multiple addresses are not supported'). 2.4.20-r0, built from CUPS 2.4.20, is the first fixed build.

CVE-2026-105326 (GHSA-r4wf-366f-f6g3): in OpenPrinting CUPS 2.4.7 to 2.4.19, the scheduler accepts any address in a mailto: notify-recipient-uri and the mailto notifier passes it to sendmail as a command-line argument, so a recipient beginning with '-' is read as a sendmail option; with a traditional sendmail that honours -C this can lead to command execution as the CUPS filter user. It is fixed in CUPS 2.4.20 by validating notification addresses in notifier/mailto.c: https://github.com/OpenPrinting/cups/security/advisories/GHSA-r4wf-366f-f6g3, https://github.com/OpenPrinting/cups/commit/611d1bd3bdf832363832383567906a6d7fd6c47d. Debian lists trixie's 2.4.10-3+deb13u2 as vulnerable and fixes it in 2.4.20-1 for unstable: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-105326. DHI publishes four rebuilds of Debian's cups 2.4.10-3+deb13u2 for Debian 13 (amd64 and arm64). Checked each of their cups-daemon packages: every one records the backport of the upstream fix in its Debian changelog, and its /usr/lib/cups/notifier/mailto carries the new address validation. The lowest of them is the fixed version in this range. The earlier rebuilds, no longer in the repository, were built before the backport was added and stay on the affected side.
